newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares rise but lack trend, Ericsson gains.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares rise but lack trend, Ericsson gains.

text.p: Swedish share prices opened slightly higher on Thursday, boosted by gains in telecoms group Ericsson and by a near record close by Wall Street overnight.
The Stockholm bourse general index was 0.23 percent higher at 3017.08 at 0820 GMT.
Brokers were mixed on where the market would end and said the trend was hard to call considering the U.S. holiday. But they agreed it would end on the positive side.
"It's a half day in the U.S.. You will see people avoiding risk today," one Stockholm broker told Reuters.
Drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn dipped 0.5 to 276 crowns.

The company said second quarter results were unlikely to match those of the first quarter, when it posted a profit of 37 U.S. cents per share while also announcing a company restructure. Brokers said this hardly came as a surprise.
"There are not many firms that have not revised their expectations downward," one said.

Telecoms group Ericsson traded two crowns higher at 276, helped by news of its $106 million deal with Chilean long-distance provider Entel Chile SA and another major GSM expansion contract in China worth $110 million.
